Today's big story: Could Anthropic Stock Fall 25%?

Two companies in the same industry grew their sales at about the same pace over the last three years. Yet over the five years to November 2026, one stock rose 135.7% and the other fell 21.9%. International Business Machines (IBM) delivered the gain, while Cognizant Technology Solutions (CTSH) suffered the decline. So where do you think the gap came from: faster growth, bigger profits, or investors paying more?

Who Has Beaten Cognizant Over Five Years?

Among companies whose three-year sales growth was close to Cognizant's, one stands out: IBM. Its stock beat Cognizant's by a wide margin. Across the whole industry, Cognizant stock landed near the middle, beating 16 of the 30 companies in its industry over those five years.

Cognizant stock sits 157.6 points behind IBM's over five years. If much of your savings is in Cognizant, that is a long stretch of falling behind to keep sitting through. Cognizant's five-year fall was close to its industry's middle. The median stock in the industry fell 22.6% over the same five years, so IBM is the one that stands out.

Did IBM Grow Faster Than Cognizant?

Over the last three years, only a little. IBM's sales grew 4.5% a year on average, against 4.1% for Cognizant. That is about the same pace.

The two businesses also sell different things. IBM sells software such as Red Hat, consulting, and the servers and storage that big clients use to run their key work. Cognizant sells technology services. Its Health Sciences business and its Financial Services business each brought in about 30% of its 2025 sales.

Where Did The Gap Come From?

The gap came from both bigger profits and what investors pay for them. From the four quarters to September 2021 to the four quarters to September 2026, IBM's earnings per share rose 121.7%, against 54.8% for Cognizant. These are figures as first reported, and IBM's are not like for like. Its 2021 figure still included Kyndryl, the business it spun off in November 2021.

Cognizant's operating margin rose 1.8 points over the same five years. That helped its profit per share grow faster than its sales. Net income rose 37.1%, and the share count fell 14.4%, so each share got more of the profit. The share count compares fiscal Q3 2021 with fiscal Q3 2026 only, so these two figures do not combine exactly into the rise in earnings per share.

Today's big story: Could Anthropic Stock Fall 25%?

Investors holding IonQ (IONQ) have endured a painful year. The stock lost 50.9% over the past twelve months, compared with an 11.0% return for the S&P 500. Yet the business itself is moving the other way. On November 5, 2026, management reported IonQ's sixth record quarter of revenue in a row. That divergence makes selling a difficult call. So how much are buyers paying today for each dollar IonQ sells?

IonQ stock lost 50.9% in one year, while the S&P 500 returned 11.0%. A fall that deep hurts most when too much of your savings sits in one stock. The Trefis High Quality (HQ) Portfolio holds 30 quality companies in equal weight, and has returned more than 105% since its September 2020 launch. Look inside HQ.

How Much Are You Paying For IonQ's Sales?

Investors are paying 24.0 times IonQ's revenue over the past twelve months, compared with 3.1 times for the S&P 500. That multiple represents the company's market value divided by a year of sales. At that level, buyers appear to be paying mostly for sales IonQ has yet to make.

The reported profit does not change that picture. IonQ posted net income of $255 million over the past twelve months, even though its operations lost $1,270 million. Management said its third-quarter profit of $564 million included an $896 million non-cash gain from a change in the market value of its warrants. The profit therefore came from an accounting gain, not from selling quantum computers.

How Fast Is IonQ's Business Really Growing?

IonQ's revenue grew 193.1% a year on average over the past three years, from a small base, compared with 6.5% for the S&P 500. Third-quarter revenue reached $174 million, up 336% from a year earlier. Part of that increase was acquired, however. The total includes two months of SkyWater, the chip foundry IonQ bought at the end of July.

Without the foundry, growth is still steep. Management said the IonQ Platform segment, which excludes the SkyWater foundry, brought in $90.3 million in the quarter, up 127%. On the same call, management raised its 2026 revenue forecast to $505 million to $515 million. Its earlier forecast was $450 million to $460 million.

IonQ Has Orders And Cash, But Deep Losses

Demand provides the case for holding the stock. Management said IonQ has sold out all of its 2027 capacity for its Superion 256 quantum computers. The company also ended the third quarter with $1.2 billion in remaining performance obligations, representing contracted work it has yet to deliver.

Why Did Rubrik Stock Jump?

Today's big story: Could Anthropic Stock Fall 25%?

Rubrik (RBRK) stock rose 9.3% on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.2%. That day, the company said its data protection product now covers a Microsoft database. Most other systems software stocks worth $2 billion or more rose too. Two of its peers climbed as well, Palo Alto Networks by 9.9% and CommVault Systems by 6.3%. Rubrik's own news was a modest product update, and it came on a strong day for software stocks. Here is what Rubrik announced and how its gain compares with its peers.

What Did Rubrik Announce On November 18?

On November 18, Rubrik said its Rubrik Cloud Data Protection now covers Microsoft Azure Cosmos DB. That is Microsoft's fully managed database for building modern apps, including AI apps. Rubrik keeps an independent, air-gapped copy of the systems on Azure, meaning a copy cut off from the network.

On the August 27 call, management named data protection as one of three product lines, with Identity Resilience and agent security. Subscriptions generate most of Rubrik's revenue. During the second quarter of fiscal 2027, subscription revenue accounted for $407.2 million of the $427.3 million in total revenue. By the end of that quarter, subscription ARR, the yearly value of its subscriptions, reached $1.66 billion. That was up 33% from a year earlier.

Did Rubrik Rise Alone Or With Other Software Stocks?

Rubrik climbed with the systems software sub-industry, but by much more than the typical stock in it. Out of the 28 other companies worth $2 billion or more in that sub-industry, 23 rose. Their median gain was 3.0%, making Rubrik's gain about three times as large. Ten of them gained 5% or more, including CrowdStrike and Fortinet.

The five companies on Rubrik's peer list split. Palo Alto Networks and CommVault Systems rose, while Dell Technologies, NetApp and International Business Machines fell. The SPDR technology sector fund (XLK) gained 0.3%.

Where Rubrik Stock Stands After The Jump

A gain this size is not rare for Rubrik. The stock had five rises at least this large in the prior 365 days. Its last move this big was an 11.1% fall on November 5, 2026.

Over the past year, Rubrik returned 57.8%, against 11.0% for the S&P 500. The six months to November 18 brought a 64.4% return. The past month brought a 4.0% loss, a smaller drop than the S&P 500's 5.0% fall. The stock closed at $110.00, sitting below its highest close of the past year, $136.00 on October 28, 2026. It is still far above its low of $43.81 on April 10, 2026.

BMO Demonstrates Quantum Utility in Machine Learning Application Using IBM Quantum Computers

BMO
IBM
BMO
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Quantum computing shows promise to help identify the most important information in complex datasets, allowing AI models to uncover useful insights with less data.

Potential banking applications include more accurate client modeling, improved risk assessment and detection, and more personalized client experiences.

Achievement positions BMO among a small group of global financial institutions exploring real-world quantum applications in the near term.

TORONTO and CHICAGO and SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 19, 2026 /CNW/ -- BMO today announced it has demonstrated quantum utility in a machine learning application using IBM quantum computers, meaning the work was performed reliably at a scale beyond what exact traditional computing methods can practically reproduce. The work explores how quantum computing could help AI models identify which information matters most in complex datasets, potentially allowing them to uncover useful insights with less data than traditional approaches.

Dr. Kristin Milchanowski, Chief AI & Quantum Officer, BMO, in front of an IBM Quantum System Two at the IBM Thomas J Watson Research Center in Yorktown Heights, New York.

Over time, that capability could have applications across banking, including more accurate client modeling, improved risk assessment and detection, and more personalized client experiences.

Developed in collaboration with the Democritus University of Thrace (DUTH), using IBM quantum computers, including the latest IBM Quantum Nighthawk r2 processor, and reviewed by IBM's quantum research team, the achievement marks an important step in bringing quantum computing closer to practical use in financial services and ultimately creating value for clients and shareholders.

This project is part of BMO's broader strategy to responsibly apply quantum technologies to AI and machine learning applications.

"Demonstrating quantum utility is an important milestone for BMO and an exciting step forward for the broader financial services industry," said Kristin Milchanowski, Chief AI and Quantum Officer and Director, BMO Institute for Applied Artificial Intelligence & Quantum. "While we remain in the early stages of application development, these projects show how quantum computing can help solve business problems in new ways. This work builds on years of research, collaboration and innovation focused on identifying practical applications that create value for clients, employees and shareholders."

As an early investor in quantum research and one of a small number of global financial institutions applying quantum computing to real-world challenges, BMO continues to focus on practical and responsible innovations that create value for clients.
